question: A 16-year-old boy presents to the emergency department with abdominal pain and tenderness. The pain began approximately 2 days ago in the area just above his umbilicus and was crampy in nature. Earlier this morning, the pain moved laterally to his right lower abdomen. At that time, the pain in the right lower quadrant became severe and constant and woke him up from sleep. He decided to come to the hospital. The patient is nauseous and had a low-grade fever of 37.8°C (100.1°F). Other vitals are normal. Upon physical examination, the patient has rebound tenderness but a negative psoas sign while the remaining areas of his abdomen are non-tender. His rectal exam is normal. Laboratory tests show a white cell count of 15,000/mm3. Urinalysis and other laboratory findings were negative. What conclusion can be drawn about the nerves involved in the transmission of this patient’s pain during the physical exam?

options.opa: His pain is mainly transmitted by the right splanchnic nerve.
options.opb: His pain is transmitted bilaterally by somatic afferent nerve fibers of the abdomen.
options.opc: His pain is transmitted by somatic afferent nerve fibers located in the right flank.
options.opd: His pain is transmitted by right somatic nerve fibers.
options.ope: His pain is transmitted by the pelvic nerves.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Abdominal pain localized to right lower quadrant" -> "suggests irritation of peritoneum" -> "peritoneal irritation often involves somatic nerves" -> "pain likely transmitted by right somatic nerve fibers" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Crampy pain above umbilicus" -> "pain migrates to right lower abdomen" -> "migration of pain suggests appendicitis" -> "appendicitis involves somatic nerve fibers" -> "pain transmitted by right somatic nerve fibers" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Rebound tenderness in right lower quadrant" -> "indicates peritoneal irritation" -> "peritoneal irritation involves somatic afferent pathways" -> "pain likely transmitted by right somatic nerve fibers" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Nausea and low-grade fever present" -> "suggests inflammatory process" -> "inflammatory processes often involve somatic nerves" -> "pain likely transmitted by right somatic nerve fibers" -> 75%

CHAIN: "Negative psoas sign" -> "indicates no iliopsoas irritation" -> "pain not from retroperitoneal structures" -> "pain likely from right lower quadrant" -> "transmitted by right somatic nerve fibers" -> 80%
analysis: The patient's presentation is consistent with acute appendicitis, where the initial visceral pain from the inflamed appendix is transmitted via the splanchnic nerves. As the inflammation progresses and irritation of the parietal peritoneum occurs, somatic pain fibers become involved, particularly from the right lower quadrant. The rebound tenderness indicates irritation of the parietal peritoneum, which is innervated by somatic nerves. Therefore, the pain is primarily transmitted by somatic afferent nerve fibers from the right lower quadrant, not the splanchnic nerves or pelvic nerves.
